import html # Pre‑defined HTML template for a blog post. # It should contain two placeholders `{title}` and `{body}` where the sanitized # title and body will be inserted. BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def format_post_content(post_title: str, post_body: str) -> str: """ Formats a user‑submitted blog post for safe display on a webpage. Parameters ---------- post_title : str The headline or title of the blog post. post_body : str The full text content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A sanitized, HTML‑formatted string containing the blog post. Notes ----- - Both title and body are escaped using :func:`html.escape` to prevent cross‑site scripting (XSS) attacks. - The resulting string is inserted into the global :data:`BLOG_FORMAT` template. Raises ------ TypeError If either ``post_title`` or ``post_body`` is not a string. """ if not isinstance(post_title, str): raise TypeError("post_title must be a string") if not isinstance(post_body, str): raise TypeError("post_body must be a string") # Escape HTML special characters to prevent XSS. safe_title = html.escape(post_title, quote=True) # The body might contain line breaks; we preserve them by converting # newlines to
tags after escaping. escaped_body = html.escape(post_body, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") # Insert sanitized content into the template. return BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=escaped_body)
